Show activity dates in the discovery report (#21)

Follow-up to the review of #18. The discovery report's New affiliations
and Affiliation changes tables now show each contributor's first and
last tracked activity (commits, opened pull requests, and reviews), so a
reviewer can see which past activity an undated entry would cover.
Reviews now also count toward the first activity that starts an old
dated period when a change is applied. New companies get their canonical
name written unquoted like hand-written entries, quoted only when YAML
would read it differently.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

Pin the toolchain, centralize dependencies, harden CI (#1)

- `rust-toolchain.toml` pins Rust 1.99 with rustfmt, clippy, and the
wasm32 target; it is the only place the version is set.
- Every dependency is declared in `[workspace.dependencies]`; crates use
`workspace = true`. Dropped the unused `thiserror`. `Cargo.lock` is
unchanged.
- Workflows use `actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain`, pin every
action by commit SHA (Node 24 versions), and default to a read-only
token; only the sync and deploy jobs get write access. Dropped
`configure-pages`, which was unused.

Deduplicate the Rust code and speed up the slower queries (#30)

Review of the Rust crates for duplicated code and performance.

Deduplication: `normalized_ai_name` existed in both crates (the
collector now reuses the core one); commit trailers were parsed and
resolved three times per commit and are now resolved once in `Facts`;
the four copies of the AI author / co-author / assistant loop became
`CommitAi::attributions` and `roles` with an `AiRole` enum; shared
helpers replaced repeated commit JSON rows, repository option lists,
branch views, repository labels, the branch filter index, the clock, URL
host parsing, and new-company construction in discovery.

Performance in the browser queries: contributor history rendered JSON
for every matching commit before keeping 100 and now renders only those
100 (15 ms to 2 ms for the heaviest contributor); rankings sort with
cached keys instead of re-folding names per comparison; identity kinds
are parsed once at load; the companies page keys repository totals by
index instead of cloned strings. Across 529 API URLs against the current
data the total median time went from 826 ms to 693 ms, and every
response is byte-identical except the overview repository dropdown,
which is now sorted by name like the other pages.

Pin binaryen and smoke-test the built site (#27)

The published site fails to start with "WebAssembly.Table.grow(): failed
to grow table by 4". Ubuntu's binaryen (108), installed by the sync
workflow, rewrites the __wbindgen_externrefs export to point at the
fixed-size funcref table instead of the growable externref table, so
wasm-bindgen's startup cannot grow it. Optimizing the same module with
binaryen 133 keeps the export on the externref table.

The workflow now downloads binaryen release 133 from GitHub and verifies
its SHA-256 instead of using the Ubuntu package. scripts/build-site.sh
ends with a Node smoke test (scripts/smoke-site.mjs) that starts the
module, loads the snapshot, and answers a dashboard query, so a module
that cannot start fails the deploy job. Locally the smoke test fails on
the 108 build with the same error and passes on unoptimized and 133
builds.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

Do not mention accounts in the discovery report (#12)

GitHub emails every account mentioned in a pull request description, and
the discovery report linked contributors with a leading at sign.
Accounts are now plain links to their GitHub profiles, and profile text
that may contain handles (profile companies, unknown organizations,
alias values) is quoted in code spans, where GitHub does not create
mentions. A test fails if the report has an at sign outside a code span.
The Copilot review comment still mentions Copilot on purpose.

Group AI models by major version and parse tool/model trailers (#31)

The AI model list had a dozen Claude rows for point releases (Opus 4.5,
4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 5, 5.5, Sonnet 4.5, 4.6, Fable 5, 5.1) and two broken
rows such as "2.1.81 / Claude Opus 4.6".

Models are now grouped by family and major version: `Opus 4.5` and `Opus
4.6` share the key `claude:opus 4` and show as "Opus 4". A trailing
dotted version is the only thing collapsed, so "Gemini 2.5 Pro" and
"gpt-5-codex" are unchanged. The exact version is kept on the AI
identity and the provider page lists the versions seen for each model,
for example "Opus 4 (4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8)".

Trailers in the form `Claude Code 2.1.81 / Claude Opus 4.6` now take the
model from the part that names a provider; a bare tool version such as
`Claude Code 2.1.81` counts as an unspecified model.

With the current data the list goes from 17 rows to 9. The snapshot
format version is bumped for the new field, and model page URLs change
(`claude:opus 4 5` becomes `claude:opus 4`).

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

Drop the CI dispatch for the discovery pull request (#10)

The `ci.yml` run that `discovery-pr.sh` dispatched never reported checks
on the pull request; the required checks come from the pull request CI
run, which GitHub holds for approval when the workflow pushes. This

version is bumped.
